title: Install field standup: alignment + tech debt log (Jun 29 2027)
body:
Weekly field install standup notes — purpose: align on customer installs, surface blockers that need cross-team escalation, and keep a running log of tech-debt items we should triage into sprints.

Date: 2027-06-29
Attendees: Nora Kim (owner), Diego Mendez (network lead), Priya Singh (install PM), Ethan Zhao (SRE), Lina Alvarez (solutions eng), plus field engineers on call: Sam R., Mei W., Jorge L.

High-level summary
- Install cadence: 4 active installs this week (2 VPC, 2 on-prem). Pull-forward for one VPC scheduled to Aug due to customer procurement — this frees a small slot next week for urgent escalations.
- Biggest systemic risk: networking failures caused by non-standard BGP configs at two customers (see NET-871).
- Tech debt highlighted: runbook gaps around KV cache warmup and node replacement; these delays are causing repeated 30–45m install overruns.

Customer-by-customer notes
1) AtlasHealth (on-prem) — status: in progress
   - Current: preflight done; hit repeat failure during node join step when applying kernel parameter tuning (sysctl). Install paused.
   - Observed: kernel bump script (scripts/install/kernel_tune.sh) sets vm.max_map_count too high on older kernel, causing k8s kubelet restart loop.
   - Ticket: PD-2345 (install-blocker: kernel tune causing kubelet restart) — owner: Sam R.
   - Action items: revert kernel tuning script for older kernels and add version guard; deliver hotfix by 2027-07-01. Diego to review patch.
   - Risk: customer is near end of maintenance window; we must finish node join before EOD 2027-07-02 or rebook with penalty.

2) Picarro Labs (VPC) — status: validation
   - Current: networking validated but observed inter-AZ latency spikes impacting model warmup times.
   - Observed: transient route flaps traced to customer-managed NAT gateways; intermittent TCP resets during large artifact pulls.
   - Ticket: NET-871 — owner: Diego Mendez; escalated to cloud provider/partner.
   - Action items: temporary mitigation: reduce concurrency for artifact pulls and enable retry with backoff in install agent; Priya to submit PR for agent change (ref: GITHUB:repo/infra#482).
   - Note: Sales wants a postmortem for customer; keep exec summary short.

3) Redwood Internal — staging on-prem lab (internal replica) — status: remediation
   - Current: node replacement exercise uncovered missing step in runbook: how to restore KV cache snapshot when the previous node had a different quantization config.
   - Impact: incomplete cache restore leads to cold-start latency for first 500 requests.
   - Action items: Lina to update runbook section 4.2 with explicit sequence for snapshot compatibility and add validation checks to mkcache tool. Target: 2027-07-05.

4) Zephyr Analytics (on-prem edge) — status: blocked (customer network)
   - Current: physical site NAT config uses carrier-grade NAT leading to ephemeral port exhaustion during container start.
   - Observed: failed healthchecks on control-plane connection; field engineer Jorge reported multiple restarts.
   - Action items: request customer networking team to enable port masquerading or provide static NAT ranges; escalate to CSM for contractual change. Lina to own customer comms.

Cross-team blockers & escalations
- Escalate NET-871 to partner network team for persistent flaps; need provider-side packet captures. Diego to coordinate.
- Need security sign-off on the temporary artifact pull retry change (low risk, but changes agent behavior). Submit SEC-approval ticket by 2027-06-30.
- Procurement timing: AtlasHealth procurement window closing — CS needs a clear plan if we miss maintenance window. Priya to sync with CSM today.

Tech debt log (operationally urgent)
- TD-01: Runbook: node-replace procedure lacks explicit KV snapshot compatibility check. Impact: repeated cold starts. Proposed fix: add compatibility check, fallback restore path, and automate validation. Owner: Lina. Priority: high.
- TD-02: Install agent: artifact pull backoff and concurrency knobs not exposed in config. Impact: installs fail on high-latency networks. Proposed fix: expose env vars and default to conservative settings for VPC installs. Owner: Priya + Diego. Priority: high.
- TD-03: Observability: install-phase tracing spans missing for 'cache warmup' and 'kv restore'. Impact: hard to metric failure modes. Proposed fix: add spans, instrument Azure/GCE loggers, and add SLO alert for warmup time >120s. Owner: Ethan. Priority: medium.
- TD-04: Tooling: repair script for old kernels is brittle (matches on distro string). Need to rewrite to check kernel version numeric. Owner: Sam. Priority: medium.

Quick metrics snapshot (this week)
- Average install time (completed): 3h 12m (target 2h) — regressions traced to cache warmup and node join failures.
- Install success rate (first-run): 78% (target 90%).
- Mean time to unblock (for field-reported blockers): 6.2 hours (target 4 hours).

Action items (compiled)
- Sam R.: PD-2345 hotfix for kernel tune script; patch + unit tests; due 2027-07-01.
- Diego M.: coordination with network partner for NET-871, gather packet captures; due 2027-07-02.
- Priya S.: PR for install-agent backoff/concurrency knobs; include test plan and SEC ticket; due 2027-07-03.
- Lina A.: runbook update for KV snapshot compatibility; add verification checklist; due 2027-07-05.
- Ethan Z.: add tracing spans for cache warmup and kv restore; update dashboards; due 2027-07-06.
- Nora K.: prepare short exec brief for customer-facing Picarro postmortem and share w/ GTM; due 2027-07-02.

Meeting notes / discussion fragments (raw)
- "Notes to self: need a reliable way to detect 'old kernel' vs 'new kernel' rather than distro string match — use /proc/version or uname -r parse." — Sam
- "If we push agent retry changes, make sure we have opt-out flag for customers who want deterministic installs." — Lina
- "We should consider a small 'pre-pull' service that downloads large artifacts at low concurrency before maintenance window starts to avoid artifact stalls." — Diego (brainstorm)
- "Reminder: update customer-facing runbook excerpt for CS so they can set expectations during maintenance windows." — Priya

Decisions made
- Temporary mitigation accepted for Picarro: reduce concurrency + enable backoff for artifact pulls (agent config) — approved by SRE on call.
- Do not revert kernel-tune globally. Hotfix will add kernel-version guard and opt-out for specific customers.

Open questions
- Can procurement at AtlasHealth grant a 2-hour buffer if we need to rebook? (CS to confirm)
- Do we want to make conservative install defaults for all VPC installs to avoid flaps at the cost of slightly longer installs? (product decision)

Next steps & cadence
- Standup cadence: keep 3x / week (M/W/F) for next two weeks while we burn down TD-01/TD-02.
- Next sync: 2027-07-01 09:30 PT (focus: PD-2345 status + NET-871 packet captures).

References / artifacts
- PD-2345: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/PD-2345
- NET-871: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/NET-871
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-infra/repo/pull/482
- Runbook (working draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/Private+Install+Playbook

End notes
- This doc is the working log for the week — will be trimmed to a customer-facing postmortem for Picarro and a short exec summary for AtlasHealth if needed. Keep edits inline; prepend initials when changing action items.

Edited by: Nora K. (2027-06-29 21:14 PT)
